evidence.method: Qualitative intrinsic-language assessment per language_quality.md fairness rules: judged against documented language design features (typing rules, control flow, references, error handling, formatting), excluding ecosystem/tooling maturity.

metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.normalized_score_rationale: Net effect places Quidra in the upper-middle band (62/100): more explicit than Python, comparable to Rust/Kotlin, more concise than C++/Java for equivalent tasks.
raw_observations: Requires explicit parameter and return types, adding verbosity versus fully-inferred languages, though 'auto' allows local inference in clear cases.
Compound assignment operators and 'elif' reduce repetition versus manual chains found in stricter C-style languages.
Built-in array combinators (.append, .concat, .sorted()) avoid hand-written loops for common operations.
Union return types (T | error, T | none) with 'try expression' propagation give concise error handling comparable to Rust's '?' operator.
Explicit reference syntax (&storage, const T &view) requires annotation at every function boundary, reducing terseness versus implicit-reference languages.
String interpolation with structured numeric format specifiers is compact versus manual format-string construction.
No implicit numeric conversions and mandatory definite-initialization add small amounts of explicit code versus auto-coercing languages.
Indentation-based blocks remove brace/end-keyword boilerplate typical of C-family languages.

metric.readability.normalized_score_rationale: Design emphasizes explicitness, exhaustiveness, and visible mutation/aliasing authority, comparable in rigor to Rust/Kotlin-tier statically typed languages. Scored in the upper band (78/100).
raw_observations: Mandatory explicit types on declarations and signatures improve self-documentation.
Exhaustive 'match' over T | name | none forces all cases into visible source.
Explicit &, const T&, and T& distinctions make aliasing/mutation authority visible at every call site.
Distinct uppercase bitwise keywords (AND, OR, XOR) versus boolean 'and'/'or' remove a common C-family confusion.
Named arguments and required-before-defaulted parameter ordering improve call-site readability.
Named escape sequences instead of backslash escapes improve readability of string literals.
Reserved-identifier and no-shadowing rules reduce naming-confusion bugs.
Language-enforced uniform indentation guarantees consistent formatting.

evidence.source: repo/docs/spec/llm-guide.md and language.md (Quidra canonical language spec). The Quidra benchmark program root (tests/benchmark/quidra) referenced by primary.json config was not among this worker's readable sandbox paths (only repo/docs, template/programs, template/workloads readable), so evidence is drawn from the canonical language specification documents.
